Subject: MAP kickoff + acceptance criteria (Pharmexa POC)

Thanks Olga/Marissa — good to reconnect.

We’re getting internal approval to start the 6-week Pharmexa POC and Procurement asked that we lock down the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and acceptance tests before the kickoff on May 4. High-level asks from our side:
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 1–2k QPS synthetic load (per our staging sim).
- Accuracy: intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on the benchmark prompts we shared.
- Cost guardrail: token cost per 10k interactions not to exceed $120.
- Security/compliance: audit logs + SOC2 evidence for the test window, and an agreed data retention policy.

Can you share a compact acceptance test matrix and a go/no-go checklist we can route to our Legal/Procurement? We’ve attached our internal MAP draft (Pharmexa_MAP_v0.9.pdf).

Thanks — Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Product, Pharmexa

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + acceptance criteria (Pharmexa POC)

Emma — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what we expected. Quick proposal below:

Summary of proposed acceptance tests (high level):
1) Latency smoke: 95th percentile measured across three 15-minute ramp windows at 1k/2k QPS; pass if <= 350ms in at least 2/3 windows.
2) Accuracy check: run your benchmark prompt set (n=2,000) against the staged model; compute intent F1 and entity precision/recall. Pass if intent F1 >= 0.88 and entity precision >= 0.80.
3) Functional regression: 200 curated prompts covering edge cases; manual spot-check pass rate >= 90%.
4) Cost simulation: replay 10k representative interactions using production pricing profile — pass if token cost <= $120.
5) Security gating: audit-log export validation (log completeness for request/response IDs) and KMS proof-of-rotation snapshot.

Exit gates (recommendation):
- Blocker: any data residency or encryption requirement not satisfied (fail immediate).
- Major: accuracy or latency misses that exceed tolerances by >20% after two remediation runs.
- Minor: cost overrun forecast; allow 1 mitigation run with optimized batching/quantization.

Action items and timeline (suggested):
- Apr 28: Redwood to share a concise acceptance matrix + test plan (redwood-acceptance-tests.xlsx).
- May 4: POC kickoff (initial baseline runs).
- Week 2 (May 11–14): Latency/accuracy smoke runs.
- Week 4 (May 25–28): Final acceptance window and sign-off.

I attached the acceptance matrix and a small audit-log sample we’ll use for integration verification. Ben will lead the test automation runs and work with your SRE.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple pragmatic clarifications from the success-playbook perspective:
- For the latency smoke, we should include a warm-up phase (KV cache priming) — measure cold vs warmed 95p and report both. Suggest labeling acceptance rows: Cold95 / Warm95 so stakeholders see variability.
- For the accuracy benchmark, please include a small holdout set (n=250) we keep secret for final verification to avoid overfitting; results only shared at final sign-off.
- Audit logs: request/response IDs must correlate with user IDs for at least 99% of events in the sample window; list exact fields in the matrix.

On exit gates: propose allowing one operational mitigation window (48–72 hrs) for major incidents (e.g., model instability) where Redwood provides a rollback plan or model variant to meet SLAs. After that window, failure becomes a non-acceptance.

Timing note for procurement sign-off: Procurement asked for an internal review buffer — if we want a May 28 sign-off, legal/procurement need the acceptance matrix by Apr 28 COB. Can we meet that?

Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[inline: quoted — Olga’s acceptance matrix attached for legal.]

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement is supportive of the plan with two small asks before we route to Legal:
1) Update the cost guardrail to show both the baseline token cost ($120 per 10k) and a worst-case cap ($160) with an explicit mitigation run if forecasted to exceed the baseline.
2) Include a short clause in the MAP that Redwood will provide an audit-log extract (sample) within 24 hours of any request during the acceptance window — we need this for our internal auditors.

If those two items are reflected in the matrix and we get the final matrix by Apr 28 COB, we’ll commit to target sign-off on May 28 and move the kickoff to May 4 as planned.

Procurement Team
